When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training for fighting at the age of 18. Before that, I used to play soccer, but I was looking for an individual sport where I can rely on myself. So I started with boxing training. It became boring, so I made the switch to MMA.

Training: Healthy breakfast before 1st session, rest, healthy lunch before 2nd session, healthy & light dinner

What ranks and titles have you held?

  • WFMC World Champion at LHW
  • AFC Austrian Champion at LHW
  • Ranked No. 12 in Western Europe at LHW (tapology)

Do you have any heroes? Gökhan Saki

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It makes me proud to represent my country Türkiye in the UFC. I want to become the 1st Turkish born UFC Champion. I want to put my country on the map and inspire all the young guys and girls. It would be a massive push for the MMA landscape in Türkiye.

What was your job before you started fighting? Car mechanic

Favorite grappling technique: Pinning and controlling

Favorite Striking technique: Left hook, right high kick

When and why did you start training for fighting?  I was born into it.  My father was a kickboxer from Chile.  I've been training in the gym since I could walk.

What ranks and titles have you held?  Lux Fight League - 155lb Title; Ranked #2 in Mexico for Pro Welterweights, Ranked #15 in Latin America (rankings according to Tapology).  Various regional titles in Mexico and Chile.

Do you have any heroes?  My father - He is the person that I look up to most.  God - Religion is a very important part of my life.  My faith has made me into the person I am today.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?  It's something I have been working for my entire life.  It's inevitable I will be there and will be a UFC champ one day.

What was your job before you started fighting?  I have been dedicated to become a professional athlete all of my life.  I moved to the United States at age 16 to pursue my career of fighting and moved to Chicago to train with Mike Valle at age 17.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition?  35 wins, 0 losses, 1 tie in amateur kickboxing.  National Chilean kickboxing champ at age 14.

Favorite grappling technique:  Guillotine

Favorite Striking technique: High kick

Personal Life / Background: I’m happily married and today I’m the father of two beautiful children: Santino, who is one year old, and Amara, who is just one month old. Life has been busy, but there’s nothing more beautiful than enjoying my family every day. Bucky, our dog, is also part of our household. As for hobbies, I’ve always liked gaming, but these days with two small kids I don’t have much time to play.

TRAINING: 9:00 am is the first training session, right now I am going to my Tuesday sparring session, right after 12:00 I have Jiu-jitsu, then I go home to rest until 6pm because I have to hit mitts. Tuesdays and Thursdays are like that. The other days I add conditioning instead of sparring.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I played soccer until I was 19 years old, Then I watched Royce Gracie fighting in the UFC and fell in love with this sport. I began fighting in 2004 and I never stopped.

What ranks and titles have you held? I am a pro fighter since 2004, with many BJJ titles, including the European championship, Brazilian championship, and many others. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt.

Do you have any heroes? God, Jesus, my wife and my three sons.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It is big for me, and I got here by working hard. Since 2000 when I first started BJJ, this was my target, and this is huge for me. I will work hard to fight great and stay in the UFC. I want to finish my career as a fighter here.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I started in the university two times - once I spent almost five months studying journalism, and the other time was publicity, but both times I had to choose training or studying; then I quit the university.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked in a bank for two years because I was living alone in Belo Horizonte, and I had to work to keep my training going. But in my head I never had the will to work in something else; fighting was always my main goal.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? I fought in more than 20 different countries, and today I have a lot of life experience because I am a fighter. This is the most important accomplishment that I could have.

Favorite grappling technique: Triangle choke

Favorite striking technique: Kicks

The main event in the life of Ismael de Jesus (Marmota) had no gloves or an opponent, but he beat a rough childhood and became a high-level athlete.

“My dream as a child was to have jeans and boots,” he says, but his biological family didn’t have very good financial conditions, sometimes spending weeks surviving only on the fruit from trees around the neighborhood. Things started to get better when he was adopted by his Portuguese father - a veteran of the war against Portugal and Angola - and mother, who passed away when he was 14. His first months in school showed that he was very agressive and had a lot of energy. To channel all this, his father made him go to judô and capoeira lessons. “I was in a lot of trouble, and martial arts made me calmer.”

After several fights and arrests, Marmota set up a company of equipmentfor air compressors and started making money, about 10,000 reais per month. But his dream of being a professional fighter was speaking louder. To assure that he had some free time to train, he started saying to his clients that he needed to visit his provider in the next town. Eventually, he decided to sell the company and take his chances on MMA in Rio de Janeiro. “Many people called me crazy, because no one could understand why I was selling a company that was doing fine.”

He used to train at Nova União in Goiania, but packed his bags and left to Rio. The first days were complicated, as he couldn’t understand why people didn’t have conversations and were so rude. “Once I saw a woman treating an old lady very bad, it seemed like she didn’t like her job. But MMA is the biggest team sport on the planet. You need good partners to succeed.”

When and why did you start training for fighting? ⁠I started at 19 years old because of my brother. He was involved in martial arts, so he dragged me to the gym and that’s how it started. He wanted me to learn something valuable except just lifting weights, which is what I did previous to coming to a MMA gym.

What professional titles have you held? No professional titles. I fought two times for KSW belt.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? ⁠I was Croatian national champion

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? The toughest fight so far was fighting for the KSW belt against Ibragim Chuzhigaev. Although I lost the fight, it was a five-round war and Fight of the Night, so ‘til this day it remains my toughest, but favorite, fight.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? ⁠My favorite fighter is Mirko Cro Cop Filipovic. It’s easy - he is Croatian and one of the biggest names that ever stepped into the cage.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I did start college but never finished.

What was your job before you started fighting? I never had a normal job. I did a bouncer job because it was the easiest job to combine with training.

Personal Life/Background: I am married, and I have two kids. Son and daughter - 2.5 years daughter and 7 months old son. In my free time, I like to hang out with my kids. I miss them a lot because we are far away when I go to training camps, so I want to make up time with them.

What ranks and titles have you held? 3x Max-Xtreme Champion – Mexico MMA

Do you have any heroes? I admire my family – my mom, dad, brothers and sisters

What is your favorite technique? Standup fighting – I love to kickbox

What does it mean for you to fight in the WEC? I am honored to fight in the WEC and I want my family and friends from Tijuana to be proud of my accomplishments.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No

What was your job before you started fighting? I never had a job because my family wanted me to train since they noticed I had talent.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started when I was in my teens just for discipline and the workout, but it became full time in my life.

What ranks and titles have you held? No ranks or titles

Do you have any heroes? My family

What is your favorite technique? I love it all...but triangle chokes are always fun!

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s a second chance for me to show my skills and myself on this level.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Went to college but no degree

What was your job before you started fighting? Security guard
